**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Leaf with a large, irregular dark brown to black lesion
- Prominent yellowish-green halo surrounding the dark lesion
- Dead tissue/hole near the lesion (tissue has fallen out)
- Small scattered yellow-brown spots on the rest of the leaf
- Lesion is on the upper leaf surface

**Key Matching:**
The yellowish-green halo surrounding the dark brown coalesced lesion is the hallmark of **Bacterial_Blight**. The reference images confirm this pattern — angular spots with yellowish-green halos that merge into larger dead patches, with tissue eventually falling out leaving a ragged appearance. The scattered small spots elsewhere on the leaf also match early-stage bacterial blight lesions.

This differs from Septoria (small uniform dark spots without halo) and Anthracnose (requires black acervuli/fruiting bodies on stems/pods).
